observation.visible_scene: A dark fireplace interior viewed through an arched opening, with a horizontal glowing log/ember bed at the bottom center. Two main flame clusters burn: a smaller one on the left and a larger, taller one on the right that often reaches the top edge of the opening. The surrounding brickwork and the lower frame bar stay in fixed positions.
visible_changes: The flames continuously flicker, rise, curl, split, and merge, changing shape from frame to frame without leaving the firebed.
The right-hand flame cluster remains the more vigorous and taller of the two throughout, with tongues that stretch upward and bend, sometimes forming hook-like curls.
The left-hand flame cluster also rises and deforms, its tongues shortening and lengthening and occasionally leaning toward the center.
The central log/ember bed glows and shifts brightness but stays in the same place; no translation of the fuel is visible.
A few tiny bright specks appear intermittently in the upper-left dark area, possibly drifting embers or reflections.
outside_clip_unknowns: The fuel type, ignition, and any airflow or door operation that drive the combustion are not shown.
The state of the fire before t=0 and after the final frame is unknown; the excerpt is a mid-burn segment.
uncertain_details: The exact material of the burning log cannot be confirmed.
The small bright specks in the upper left may be sparks, reflections, or sensor noise; their motion is not clearly tracked.
No camera movement is evident, but the static framing is inferred from the unchanged arch and bottom bar rather than from background parallax.
